utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Good morning. Please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. Case number IT-95-9-T, the Prosecutor against Blagoje Simic, Milan Simic, Miroslav Tadic, and Simo Zaric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The Prosecution is continuing its examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. If Your Honours please, yesterday, you made a query regarding the time frame that the witness was talking about when he was referring to this Spomen Dom meeting. I've checked the transcript. He mentioned June or late June.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Oh, yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Witness, I'd just like to go back briefly to the Spomen Dom meeting that you mentioned yesterday. You told us how you became aware of it with the posters around the town, and the attendants, the number of people who were there, the ethnic background, and some of the personalities who addressed the meeting. Were there any armed guards at the meeting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were. I saw two of them standing at the door at the entrance to the Spomen Dom.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Can you tell us if they were members of the 4th Detachment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly whether they were members of the 4th Detachment, but they were armed, and they were standing by the door.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: How long did the whole meeting take?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: The meeting lasted for a very short time. After the speech by Jovo Savic, people started leaving the meeting. I think Vlado Sesic stood there and wrote down the names of those people who had left the meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did you have to sign in or notify anyone of your attendance at the meeting, the fact that you'd gone there? For instance, sign in on a document or something like that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: You mentioned that some people did take up the invitation to take up arms. Do you know if they did that at the meeting, or was that something you learnt subsequently?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right after the meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did you consider taking up arms and relieving yourself of work obligation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. I want to ask you about the -- your commencement of work in Odzak. About when did you start going to Odzak?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sometime around the 9th, after the mosque was destroyed. That's when I started working in Odzak, the 9th, the 10th, July.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I apologise, Witness. I realise there are a number of issues on the Spomen Dom meeting that I didn't ask you about and I must ask you. I'll get on to Odzak just shortly. You said that there was a great escape that followed after the meeting in the Spomen Dom.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Can you give us an idea of the sort of numbers of men who made their escape?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Around 130 people.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: How did you become aware of it the fact that these men had escaped?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: The next day, right in the morning when we gathered in front of the local commune building.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Were people talking about it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Was the meeting ever -- sorry, the escape, rather, ever commented on over the radio?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: What did you hear said over the radio as regards this escape?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that the announcer, Mira Ljujic [phoen] said over the Radio Samac that the remaining people should be dealt with, because we were all the same, and the best thing would be to let us go down the river Sava and not across the river.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: The expression used, "go down the river Sava," can you think back and tell us precisely what the expression was that she used to describe going down the river Sava?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: That we should be killed, the rest of us.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did this radio announcer have a nickname?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: What was it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sesula [phoen].

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Following the escape, was there any change in the conditions of life for the inhabitants of Bosanski Samac, and yourself included?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I'm concerned, there were no changes. I continued working, but the families of those who had escaped were gathered up and taken to the Zasavica camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I may have asked you this, but I'd like to -- like you to remind the Chamber just again. About how long after the night of the escape, did the Zasavica roundup of civilians occur?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: One day later.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Was that commented on or mentioned in the radio, as far as you can remember?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, I'd like to turn to Odzak, please. You've told us that you started going there around the 9th and 10th of July.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And was that as part of work groups sent from Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Is it the case that you would go there, work during the day, and then return at night to Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: How were you transported to Odzak?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: By truck.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: You've mentioned earlier that there were armed guards who accompanied you on previous work assignments. Were there armed guards on your trips to Odzak?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: On these trips to Odzak, were there women workers present on the trucks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: On the way to Odzak, did the truck have to pass through checkpoints?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: In Odzak, is there a hotel?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Where did you normally assemble and report for work duty when you were going to Odzak?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: In front of the hotel.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Can you describe the scene that you saw of Odzak to the Chamber when you went there for the first time on such a work detail? What did the place look like?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was abandoned. There was a lot of destruction. A lot of houses had been burnt. I saw that the mosque had been destroyed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me. Witness, to your knowledge, do you know who was suspected of blowing up the mosque?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I learned that later on. I was not there when the mosque was destroyed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Could you tell us what you learned later?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I learned later that the army destroyed the mosque, that my fellow citizen was there when the mosque was blown up, and I heard it from him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Thank you. So when you say "the army," so you're saying the JNA blew the mosque up, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think it was the reservists who did that, because when we say -- when I say "JNA," I mean the young soldiers. And the people who were 50 years of age, I do not consider them to be members of the JNA. These were the Serb reservists, paramilitaries of sorts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If Your Honours please, I'll be leading at a later point fuller evidence of the destruction of the various religious institutions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio, you had mentioned that a couple of witnesses ago, so this will be being done with a future witness? Is that my understanding?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And this witness has got matters -- can talk about the destruction of these religious institutions as well, so there will be evidence from this particular witness on the various institutions, as much as he can tell, of course. But I will lead evidence of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes. Now, I think you said that you would report to the hotel for your work assignments. What I want to know is this: The tasks that you were assigned in Odzak, were they given to you in Bosanski Samac, or is it the case that you were taken to Odzak and there handed work assignments, there in Odzak informed of what it was that you were to do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were driven from Samac, and we were given our tasks in front of the hotel, the tasks that we were supposed to do in Odzak.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did you ever see Simo Zaric in Odzak?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: How often?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very often. Virtually every day.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Where did he have -- I'll rephrase that question. Did he have an office in Odzak?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Where?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw him often standing by the bar at the entrance, and allegedly he had an office upstairs. But he sat there at the table all the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I take it you mean the hotel?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did you ever see him issuing orders and instructions to various people around the place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did you have any idea of what sort of authority or position he held in the city of Odzak, the town of Odzak?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Tell us what you know about that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think he was -- he had the superior authority. He was in charge in Odzak.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Turn your attention now to the moments when you would be gathered in front of the hotel receiving your work assignments. Who assigned work to you? That is, who came up and orally -- and told you, actually told you, spoke to you, explaining what your work assignment would be for that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was Stojan Blagojevic. He issued orders to us, and he guarded us.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: How big was the work detail or the work group that went to Odzak? How many of you were there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Around 50 of us would gather in front of the hotel, men and women.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Now, when Mr. Stojan Blagojevic was telling the assembled people what their work would be, was Simo Zaric ever present?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: On such occasions, would he be in a position to hear what was being said to the assembled workers, in your judgement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: He probably could have heard me because he was quite near.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did you ever see any sort of communication going on, talking, exchange of documents, anything like that, at about the time that Blagojevic would hand out the work assignment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: When Simo Zaric was present at the time that work assignments were being handed out, what would he be doing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: He looked at us, and he would often say that an additional two or three people should join such and such a group or five people should go there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. What sort of work did the women do in the group that used to go to Odzak?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: They cleaned the town, did maintenance in the hotel, cleaned the police station, cooked food for the police, and cleaned the apartments of those Serbs who returned to Odzak.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And give us an idea of the sort of work that the men were engaged, not just the work that perhaps you did, but the work that you knew other men were doing. Just give us a list of the type of tasks.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: One group worked on the farm, and another group looted the town, taking things out of apartments, and I did work on the water supply system in Odzak. I did some repairs and some preparations for the re-establishment of the water supply system in Odzak.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Insofar as looting is concerned, did you participate in that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Who would decide, for example, which street or houses had to be looted?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Stojan Blagojevic led us. And before that, he had a meeting with Mr. Zaric, and that is where the orders that were issued to us stemmed from.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay. Do you know the town of Novi Grad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: During your trips and your work, labours, in Odzak, did you ever have occasion to go to Novi Grad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Do you know a gentleman named Dusko Popovic? Just answer me yes or no.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Can you tell the Chamber of the circumstances under which you went to Novi Grad.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: One day I was picked up from the water supply company in a police car, and I was driven to the hotel. Mr. Zaric then said I should go to Novi Grad to repair the hydrant line. They said I would be taken to Samac to take the materials I need and then on to Novi Grad. And then he addressed Dusko Popovic, who was a policeman of the Serb Republic - Simo Zaric addressed him - and said, "If he fails to repair it, hang him there."

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Let's go through this a little more slowly. Am I correct in understanding that you were already engaged on work at the water supply company in Odzak when a police car came to your job site, got you, and took you back to wherever Simo Zaric was, and then this conversation occurred?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Earlier in your evidence, you told us of your training as a plumber and how you had done work on domestic and industrial plumbing, appliances. Was the sort of job that you eventually did at Novi Grad something that was within your capability, something that you could do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Very well. After this conversation, or rather, after you heard the words from Mr. Zaric, "If he doesn't repair it, hang him there," were you in fact taken to Novi Grad, and did you work on some sort of water works installation there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: How long did you -- how long did you work at the job?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: That day, I worked very late. It was already dark when I finished. But I had to finish.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did you stay overnight in Novi Grad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Were you taken from the water works to Simo Zaric, where you heard his words about repairing it, and then from there, to Novi Grad, under armed guard?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. In the time that you went to Odzak, did you ever come across a gentleman named Perko? P-e-r-k-o, Perko.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did you ever do any particular jobs with him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Tell the Chamber what that particular job was.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were burning books.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay. Now, give us a bit more detail. Was this -- were you part of a work group when you did this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Was it within the town of Odzak or a neighbouring village? Where exactly was it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was in the town of Odzak.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: About how many workers were engaged in this particular task of burning books?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were about eight.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Who assigned this particular job to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the teacher by the name of Perko, a man from Montenegro. I don't know his last name.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: How was it that he could order you to do any sort of job at all? Did he hold some sort of authority in Odzak, as far as you're aware, or did he liaise with anyone? Do you know, in other words, how he acquired the authority to direct you to do a job?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: He told us then that he got his orders from the command.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Were you at the hotel or assembled at the hotel at the time that you got your orders from Perko or started off on the job with Perko?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were gathered outside the hotel. Perko picked us out. And before that, he had come out of the hotel, selected us, and we started off.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Do I understand that to mean that he had been inside the hotel first and then came out and selected you or the workers who were to accompany him? Is that a correct understanding or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And this occasion, were you assembled in front of the hotel, as you were on the other occasions when you started work in Odzak? In other words, was it part of the normal routine that you had at Odzak?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Very well. Tell the Chamber what Perko decided was your work assignment for that day.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: To take out books from various homes, houses and apartments, books written by non-Serbian authors. We were to pile them up and burn them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: First of all, the homes that you took them from, can you comment on the apparent ethnic background of the occupants of the house, if you can tell us?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those were Muslim and Croat homes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: They were presumably empty homes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Explain to the Chamber how it is that you can walk into a home and tell if it's Croat or Muslim. What sort of things do you look at to help you identify what sort of people used to live in the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is very easy to identify Croat homes. You would see the crucifix there and similar things, pictures of the Madonna and so on. And Muslim homes are also easy to tell, if you look at the furniture, the objects around.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Was there any way of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: What about the other ethnic group, the Serb houses? What would distinguish them?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I was just go to get on to that topic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I was thinking he was mentioning things you find inside the houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So perhaps they would get in and say, "Oh, this is a Serb house," and perhaps get out.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes. Or perhaps not go in at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. If there were signs outside the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes. I was about to get on to that very topic, if Your Honour pleases.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Perhaps, Witness, you heard the discussion between myself and Her Honour. And we are interested to know if there was any way of identifying a Serb house when you were carrying out this sort of --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was very easy because it was written on the door, "Don't go in. Serbian fighter," the cross with the four letters "S." A Serbian house was very easy to tell.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. By those symbols which were outside the door? Is that what you're saying, Witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's what I'm saying.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Were these symbols ever spray-painted?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Perhaps on the symbols, the things he's talking about, how you identify different homes belonging to different ethnic groups, was that always the case, even before the war? Even today is that the case? Or was it just during that period when the war -- did the differences arose 1991, for instance, up to about 1993, or is that the way people live there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think it was an abnormal way of life, and this marking of houses started in 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Just on this issue, you've mentioned that once you got inside a house, you could tell if it was Croat by various religious insignia and symbols; and once you got inside a house, you could tell if it was Muslim by the style of the house and the interior decoration, I suppose. Was that something that had always been in Bosnia that -- and long before the war, you would be able to tell if you went into a house whether it was a Croatian house or indeed a Serbian house or a Muslim house, judging by the things that you'd see inside it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. But this other phenomenon that you mentioned, the insignia, the slogans written on the front of the house that there was a Serb fighter there, and that sort of thing, was that apparent before the war, or was that something that happened during the war or started after the war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: That started during the war, the marking of houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, I gather, then, that it was easy for to you select or avoid going into, rather, Serb-occupied homes by the insignia on the outside. Was that the only thing that stopped you from mistakenly going into a Serb home?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since Stojan Blagojevic often escorted us, he knew those houses, and we didn't enter Serb houses at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did he -- on the occasions of your entering the Croat and Muslim houses, did he point out which ones were to be entered and your work done?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: We went from house to house.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. All right. Now let's get back to this episode with Perko and the books, please. I think you said that you selected books by non-Serbian authors. Were these -- what did you do with these books?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: We would stack them and then burn them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Were there individual stacks of books, or was it by bonfire, so to speak?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was more like a bonfire.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Tell the Chamber how you were policed to make sure that you chose the non-Serb books, or indeed, how you chose non-Serb books. What was it that you looked for in the book to decide if it was Serb or non-Serb?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: We would take out books, and then the teacher, Perko, would inspect them, dividing them into groups, non-Serbian writers to one side, and the other books to be burnt on the other side.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: What happened to the books that made it through this cleansing process, in other words, the Serb books?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perko, the teacher, took them, because a library was supposed to be established in Odzak.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I see. Thank you. How long did this job take?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: It took up the whole day.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know a gentleman named Fadil Mustafic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Can you tell us if he is distantly related to any of the defendants?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: He's related to Mr. Simo Zaric's wife.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: In 1992, the period of time that you were going to Odzak, about how old was he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: About 60.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And of what ethnic background was he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was a Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Was he doing forced labour assignments in Odzak?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: What sort of work was he doing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: He tuned cars in the SUP in Odzak.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did he normally reside in Bosanski Samac or elsewhere?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Bosanski Samac. That's where he resided.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: When he was working in there, did he ever stay overnight in Odzak?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: He did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did you ever hear, overhear, any conversation between Fadil Mustafic and Simo Zaric?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Can you recount that conversation to the Trial Chamber, please, as carefully as you can, what you overheard and who said what?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: One day, when we were going to lunch, Mr. Simo Zaric was sitting at his table. Fadil Mustafic approached him and asked him, "Simo, when are you going to let me go?" And he replied, "Brother" - using the word for brother-in-law - "be good and I'll let you be exchanged."

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Where was this lunch?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the hotel.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did Fadil Mustafic ever manage to get out through an exchange?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: He did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Now, how did he manage that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was together with me when we were transferred to the Batkovici camp, and he returned to Samac in 1993. Then Fadil Topcagic from Samac took him all the way to the Hungarian border, where Fadil's son, Dino, gave him 4.000 Deutschmarks and got him out, got him out of Samac.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Gave who 4.000 Deutschmark?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: To Fadil Topcagic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Is this something you heard about later?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Do you know a gentleman named Pero Krstanovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did you ever see him when you were doing labour assignments in Odzak?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did you ever hear Simo Zaric speak to him in Odzak?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Once again, please tell the Chamber of what you overheard and what happened on the occasion that Krstanovic spoke to Mr. Zaric?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't quite understand the question, I mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: In the course of your assignment in Odzak, did you ever dismantle installations in homes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did you ever dismantle any radiator systems?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Were you ever instructed by Simo Zaric to dismantle any radiator systems?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't personally, but he instructed Stojan Blagojevic and Pero Krstanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Were you present when that -- when he issued those instructions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did you in fact go on to dismantle radiator systems?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay. Well, that's the episode that I'm interested in. So let's start at the beginning, and you can tell us what you overheard and what you did.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the second house, if you go from Odzak towards the Catholic church. I dismantled the heater from the central heating system, together with the radiators. We also dismantled some of the installations because those were copper pipes, very expensive at the time, and we loaded that on the truck, driven by Pero Krstanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: What I'm actually more interested in, though, is what happened before you did the job, how you received the instructions, what you heard being said about the job, and who said it. That's what I'm interested in.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was a long time ago, but I think Mr. Simo told us to pick out the good things, and that's what we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: How many of you were engaged in this particular assignment involving these copper expensive radiator systems?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was assisted by Sead Zigic, and later more people joined us from this work detail when we were loading the heater onto the truck.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did you receive the instructions for this particular job as usual in the -- in front of the hotel in Odzak?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you could say it was in the usual way, with the proviso that Mr. Simo came personally to see us, because the house was very close to the hotel.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Do you mean he attended at the job?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did he watch what was going on?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: He just took a look, and then he went back.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Whose house was it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a Muslim home. I don't know the name of the owner.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Would Your Honours just bear with me for a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: I'd like to ask the witness a question just for clarification. It appears I think that you said that Mr. Zaric told Mr. Stojan Blagojevic and Mr. Pero Krstanovic to go and dismantle the radiators and the copper pipes. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: And then the orders that you got to go to the home and participate in that dismantling, did you get those orders from those two gentlemen, Mr. Krstanovic and Mr. Blagojevic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They were my immediate superiors, who led me wherever I was supposed to go and guarded me at the same time. They would take me to a house, and I would have to do whatever they told me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Can you tell the Chamber if after those two gentlemen, Krstanovic and Blagojevic received their orders from Mr. Zaric, were you then taken to the house to conduct the extraction of the radiator system?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. And you tell us about how the job ended. You got to the point where you said it was -- I think, it was placed on a truck. And Where was the radiator system taken after that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: To Samac, in front of Fadil Topcagic's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did you go on the truck to accompany this equipment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: What happened at Fadil Topcagic's house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's where we unloaded this, the radiators and the heater, in front of his house.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did you then drive away, leaving it there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We did not drive away because we all lived in Samac, so everybody just went back to their homes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I see. Yes. Thank you. Were you eventually arrested in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: What was the date, as far as you can recall, or the approximate period of time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was in September. I think it was the 7th.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: Just one question here. After leaving the radiator system in front of Fadil Topcagic's house, do you know what happened to that system?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Now, you told the Chamber that you started working in Odzak around the 9th and 10th of July and that you were arrested on -- in September, early September. Throughout that period of time, did you work only in Odzak, or rather, were you taken to Odzak every day, in that period of time leading right up until your arrest?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: It depended on the actual need. Sometimes they would leave me there if I had to do something for somebody in Samac.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Can you comment on whether or not you spent most of that time, that is, between early July and early September, doing work assignments in Odzak?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Do you know of a place called the Borovo factory?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Can the witness be shown Exhibit P9. I think I've got the exhibit number right. It's the photographs. I believe it's P9. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. And in particular, photograph 35.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I think it's Exhibit P14/A.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I'm grateful to the Chamber. And might I just see the photograph, perhaps, before it's handed to the witness? Would Your Honours please bear with me for one moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So the witness is being shown P14/A photograph number.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: 11, if Your Honours please. I'm sorry about the delay. I didn't have the photograph number in my notes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: All I need you to do, Witness, is just to have a look at that photograph and tell us what it depicts.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the factory of the uppers, footwear uppers, in Odzak, the Borovo factory in Odzak.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Usher. That's all I needed the witness to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did you get engaged in any work at that factory?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: What did you do there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I dismantled the machinery that was left there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Any idea who issued orders or instructions for that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know who issued the orders, but I do know who took me there to work.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Who took you there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Stojan Blagojevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: How long did the job there take?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Four to five days we worked there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And was it just a question of dismantling machinery and getting it out of the factory, taking it away?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: We also loaded the machinery onto trucks.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Where was it taken?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: To Samac.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: How long did the job take?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Four to five days, until we cleaned it all up.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And do you know what happened to the machinery that you took to Samac from the Borovo factory?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were unloaded at the Mladost factory, and then the rumour was that they went -- that the machinery was taken to Zlatibor in Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: You say "the rumour." Are you referring to what you were informed by other citizens, as to what had been the fate of the machinery?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Other citizens told me that. The people that worked with me, they had some information about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: Are we going to have evidence of a rumour?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Well, I'm not presenting it as anything other than that, if Your Honours please. That's precisely why I asked the question. And to clarify that, I am fully aware that it is regarded -- it might be regarded as hearsay in other jurisdictions, and I don't seek to present it as anything more than what it says on its face, if Your Honour pleases.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: The -- when you did the job at the factory, had the factory been damaged?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Had it been apparently damaged by war activity, by shells, bombs, bullets, that sort of thing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: In the five days that you did work there, were you or was the factory targeted or struck by shells or gunfire at all?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, Witness, you've described in detail all of the sort of work that you conducted in Bosanski Samac and neighbouring villages and in Odzak. In all of the time that you were engaged in this sort of labour, these sort of projects, did anyone ever record, write down in any way at all, the days that you worked or the hours that you worked?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: In all the time that you worked in Bosanski Samac and in Odzak, did anyone ask you how many hours you had worked or how many days you had worked?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: In all the time that you worked in Bosanski Samac and in Odzak, were you ever paid for any of the work that you did?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: In all the time that you worked in Bosanski Samac or in Odzak, did you ever see anyone being paid for the work they did or even hear of anyone being paid for the work they did?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Can the witness be shown D22 E/2 ter, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Witness, can you please just read out for the benefit of the Chamber, the title at the top of the page so that we can refresh our memories of what this document says, there not being any translation at this stage.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: "List of workers involved in the work brigade for the month of April, May, June, July, and August 1992."

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. And you will see that the pages are obviously divided into columns. At the top is an explanation of what the columns represent. Start at the left and read across and tell us what the columns are, please.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the document please be placed on the ELMO for interpreters.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: First we have the serial number, full name.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The interpreters are asking whether the document can be placed on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I've not go problem with that as far as -- unless it's under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Is it?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That document is under seal, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So we have to go into closed session.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio can you ask him when he's familiar with that sort of document, whether he's ever seen one.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can we go in closed session?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Can the witness please be shown P38 ter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: We are now in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Your Honours. May I ask the Court if this is a document under seal? Can it be --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. If we can please place it on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. Can you place the document on the ELMO so that we can see it? Good. Now, is that a -- is that document headed "Workers in the work brigade, dead or injured"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And it apparently refers to the period of time between April and August of 1992.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: It also lists the number of -- the number of workers who were killed. And you see them there: Mr. Idrizi, Mr. Nurkic, and Omeragic. First of all, can you tell us where those persons were killed, what sort of work they were doing when they were killed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Redzep Idrizi got killed while digging trenches at Zasavica. Dzevad Nurkic got killed at Pisari, also digging trenches. Fikret Omeragic got killed outside his own home in Samac. Follows a list of the wounded: Rizo Jusufovic, Fuad Bobic, Almir Kapetanovic, and Mirsad Tihic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Let's just concentrate on those killed, rather than those wounded, first of all. It says there were three people killed in that period of time, presumably while doing work. Do you know of any others, any other men, or indeed women, who were killed while carrying out work obligations or forced labour, whatever term you apply to it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Missing from this list are Ibro Ibralic, who was a courier. He got killed while delivering summons on his bicycle.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: You say he was killed while delivering summonses. What sort of summonses are you talking about there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those were summonses for the work obligation.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And can you tell us if he was killed during the period of time that is purportedly covered -- that this document purportedly covers, that is, between April and August of 1992? Was it during that period of time that he was killed, or was it outside of that period of time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was killed within this period of time indicated in the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Now look at the list of those who were wounded. Can you tell us what sort of work they were engaged in at the time that they were wounded?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: All of them were engaged in digging trenches, and that's where they got injured.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Is it the witness's assertion that they were injured by crossfire?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes, I was just going to clarify that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: You heard Her Honour's question. That's something we'd like to know, if you can tell us. What sort of activity were they engaged in at the time that they were injured?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were digging trenches. And since we were in front of the line while doing that, there was an exchange of fire in which they got wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: That applies to all four of them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And all four wounded in different -- on different occasions, as far as you're aware, or was that just the one occasion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were wounded on different occasions.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. I've finished with that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I wonder if Mr. Usher would be so kind as to retrieve that and give the witness Exhibit P39 ter, P39 ter. And I don't think this one is under seal either, so it can be placed on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. It's not under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: This document is an accounting document of some sort relating to the months between April and August of 1992. Look at the first two names there, please, Sejdinovic and Celic. It asserts that they were clerks or -- can you tell the Chamber if in that period of time, that is, April to August, they in fact were working as clerks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: What were they in fact doing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were engaged in digging trenches, and they became clerks only towards the end of the month of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: When in relation to the great escape that you've mentioned did they become clerks? Before or after?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: After that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Is the fact of their becoming a clerk and being taken off trench work in any way related to that event, the escape?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Dzemal Kapetanovic escaped, nicknamed Beg, and Saba Hudinogic, who had been clerks before they escaped.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Now, I was interested in the two men whose names appear in the document, numbers 1 and 2, Sejdinovic and Celic. You said they were clerks -- you said they became clerks but only in -- towards the end of July. What I wanted to know was whether the fact that they became clerks, Sejdinovic and Celic, did that have anything to do with that large escape of men swimming across the Sava River that you mentioned earlier in your evidence. Were the two issues in any way connected?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: They are very closely related, these events, because with the escape of the two former clerks, two vacancies appeared. The two men, Kapetanovic and Nogic, who had escaped, were educated men. I believe they were engineers. And these two on the list, Celic and Sejdinovic filled their positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you comment on the ethnic background of the people whose names are listed in P39 ter? Just run your eyes down the list, starting at 1, finishing at 9, and tell us what ethnic background those people are.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Number 1 is a Muslim; number 2, a Muslim; number 3, a Muslim; number 4, a Muslim; 5, Muslim; 6, Muslim; 7, Muslim; 8 and 9, also Muslims. All of them are Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Usher. I've finished with that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay, Witness, I want to turn now to another issue, and that is the fate of the mosque in Bosanski Samac. Let's try and get -- perhaps I'll withdraw that, and I'll ask you this: Was the mosque destroyed in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Just try and get a fix on when that occurred. If you know the precise date, of course tell us. If you can give us an approximate period of time, tell us.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was between the 27th and the 28th of July, towards the end of July, at any rate.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Can you tell us if you were still based in Bosanski Samac? And by that I mean was this before you started the regular work assignments in Odzak?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, I was working indeed in Odzak, and that event occurred during the night between the 27th and the 28th. And I worked as usual getting my work assignments outside the local community.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Do you know a gentleman named -- or rather, gentlemen named Perica Krstanovic and Marinko Stefanovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: When did -- did you ever have any dealings with them in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew them very well. Perica used to be the director of the electrical company, and Marinko was an employee with the electrical company in Samac.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: What background were they? What was their ethnic background?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did they hold any positions within any of the organs of the town, for example, the 4th Detachment or the police force, anything like that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't give you a precise answer because I don't know what kind of position they held in town after the war broke out, but I know that Perica was the director of the electrical company and Marinko was employed with the same company. Perica wore a uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: A military uniform?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did those men ever visit you at your home?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: One evening, before the mosque was destroyed, Marinko called on me. He arrived in his car, I believe it was a Zastava 128, and I saw that Perica, the director was sitting inside. They wanted me to give them my Hilti drill. Since I told them I didn't have it, they left.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Firstly, I have two questions in respect of this drill. Firstly, was it true that you didn't have such a drill? And secondly, is this drill capable of getting through concrete and stone?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: To your first question, I'll tell you: I had it, but I didn't give them because I didn't think they would return it, and it is a very expensive drill. To your second question: The answer is yes, it is used normally for drilling through concrete and stone.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Was this an unusual visit from these men, in the sense of they are not men who normally came to your house or you normally had any dealings with?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and I was surprised by their visit.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: During the night or the early morning, did you hear anything?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: That morning, I heard a loud explosion, but I didn't know what had happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did you ascertain what had happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did, later, because at that time the curfew was still on, and we were not allowed to leave our homes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I'll be asking you about the curfew later on, but at this stage tell us if you eventually left the house and ascertained what had happened in respect of that explosion.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I left my house, I met -- I ran into Suhra Porogic who told me that the mosque was destroyed. Since I was supposed to go and report for work, I took a different road past the mosque to see it. I saw that it was destroyed, and I continued walking towards the local community.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Now, do you know of a place in Bosanski Samac called the Posavka department store?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did you notice anything unusual about the Posavka department store this morning that you were -- walked past the mosque?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Tell us.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw two thin wires, one white, the other grey, going across the asphalt to the back of the department store.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Apparently leading from where to where?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the department store to the mosque.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: What did the mosque look like at the time that you saw these two wires?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was destroyed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: When you arrived at your assembly point, work assembly point, did you discuss the fate of the mosque with anyone or did anyone discuss it with you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Tell us who spoke to you, if anyone, and what exactly -- exactly they said to you on the issue of the mosque.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I talked to Kemal Mehinovic who told me that he had seen Marinko Stefanovic unrolling the wire from the back of the department store towards the mosque, and he saw another man, Perica, inside the department store, which was the origin of the explosion apparently.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Judge Williams, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: I apologise. Mr. Di Fazio, I have a question for yourself. Destruction of religious institutions. Now, this is contained in the Statute of this Tribunal and Article 3(d), violations of the laws or customs of war, ie, (d) seizure of, destruction, or wilful damage done to institutions dedicated to religion, and so on and so forth. Obviously this is based on well-known fact in international criminal law that cultural property, religious property, is protected in time of armed conflict, 1954 Hague Convention, and so on and so forth. So my question is: We have no mention in the current indictment of damage to religious institutions. So my question to you, Mr. Di Fazio, given that we are contained here by the four corners of the present third amended indictment: Are you seeking to bring destruction to the mosque and other religious institutions within count 1, persecution, based on Article 5(h) of the Statute of the Tribunal, and particularly page 5 of the indictment, paragraph 14(e), which concerns wanton and extensive destruction, plundering, and looting of the property of Bosnian Croats, Bosnian Muslims, other non-Serb civilians, including dwellings, businesses, personal property, and livestock? No mention is made of religious institutions. Are you wanting - shall we say - a more liberal reading of (e) to include religious institutions such as the mosque and the Catholic church in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes, if Your Honour pleases, as far as 14(e) is concerned, it should be covered by that particular paragraph. May I just have a moment to confer with my colleague on this, on this issue?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Your Honour's question, with the utmost respect is entirely appropriate and I think highly pertinent and needs to be answered. It does, however, take me by surprise at this point in time, and I can address you on this issue. If I could do so at a later point, it would, I think, be of benefit both to myself and to Your Honour to do that. I understand from my colleague, Mr. Weiner, that there is a recent decision that might touch upon this issue, and I would like to have an opportunity to read that. I understand it's Kupreskic. So would Your Honour be satisfied if I dealt with this question and addressed you upon it at a later stage and proceeded to take this evidence at this time?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio, I would have one other question to add to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: -- to the previous question, and then the Chamber would give you time to consider what your response to the questions would be. But the Chamber is of the view that that should be done before the cross-examination of this witness to give the Defence the opportunity to include it in their cross-examination if they so wish.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Your Honour refers to my reply to you, or any application to amend, or both? That should be done before, before any cross-examination of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, I think the reply. And if the reply will include your proposal to amend, then it better be, because it's through the evidence of witnesses that we deal with all these matters, and it is important that the Defence are notified in due time before they cross-examine. And as Judge Williams said they can decide whether to take up those matters with this witness or not to, depending on what the defences of their clients are.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes, very well. Well, in that event, might I use the rest of the day to consider our position, confer with my colleagues, and answer that inquiry tomorrow morning and give any indication on that very issue tomorrow morning?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And before Defence counsel have to stand up and cross-examine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. And before you wind up with the witness, because then it will become necessary whether or not that evidence should be elicited or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. That will be attended to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio, just the second point if you could add into your consideration of this question: Again referring to paragraph 14(e), the one I read out from the indictment --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: -- the meaning of "the property of Bosnian Croats, Bosnian Muslims," do we read in private property there or do we also read in - should we say - public property of religious institutions not owned, therefore, by individual Bosnian Muslims or Croats living in the municipality of Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: And then there is also the question of the word "including" in that portion of the indictment, whether that can be read more broadly and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes. I understand the point. And I'll address the Chamber on that, as I said, tomorrow, and before the close of this witness's evidence, his examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. And perhaps we -- you can leave that part of your examination-in-chief and move on to other matters, if there are still other matters for your examination-in-chief, so that we can move on at least for the time we have, and then adjourn, and then you can prepare yourself before you go to this particular aspect.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes, of course. So I take it that the Chamber wishes me not at this stage not to continue with any evidence on the destruction of any --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Religious.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: -- religious. Yes, very well. I can do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. I think we can include other destructions which -- other matters concerning (e), perhaps to be on the safe side, and then you move on with your examination-in-chief on other matters related to other things.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I understand. This was a very specific topic that I was going to deal with, institutions in Bosanski Samac, Odzak, the mosque, and the Catholic church in Odzak, and also the Catholic churches in some other villages. I'll skip that and move on to another topic and only get back to that after we have conferred tomorrow and I've made submissions on the issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. I thought I saw Ms. Baen or somebody from the dense standing up.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Actually, that was the issue I was going to address is that he should not go into this topic on direct, and so we are in agreement with the Court on that. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. So you can move on with examination-in-chief in other areas of the evidence of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes. The next topic that I'm going to propose to deal with, given the results of this discussion, are rapes that occurred in Odzak. And I propose to do that on the basis of the ruling that you made the other day in respect of the witness led by Mr. Weiner. It's essentially the same sort of material covered by Mr. Weiner. And I take the position that you having given the ruling, as far as that witness is concerned, it applies to whatever this witness can say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, you can go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: However, names will be mentioned of victims, and I wonder, therefore, if we should go into private session for that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Right away.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: -- and avoid names, take the risk of names being mentioned when I deal with this topic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. So we move into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. We are in open session now.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you said that trucks would pass through checkpoints on the way to and from Odzak. In the evenings, would the -- would the truck pass through checkpoints on the way back?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: On such occasions, were there ever girls or young women on the truck? And I mean of course occasions when you were there.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Who manned the checkpoints?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Serb troops.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did any of the girls or the young women ever get off at the checkpoints?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: The girls didn't get off. They were pulled off by Serbian soldiers. Three or four girls would be picked out and pulled off the truck, and we would continue on to Samac without them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: When this happened, would there be -- would you still have the guard with you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And presumably, a truck driver?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Were they locals from Bosanski Samac, the guard and the truck driver?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would very often be a member of the police or the Serbian army, and most often, it was Stojan Blagojevic who accompanied us.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Now, where was Stojan from? Was he from Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was from a village called Pisari, near Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: So essentially he was a local living in the municipality of Bosanski Samac; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Now, when these girls were taken off the truck, did he have an opportunity to see this happening?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Ever hear him complain to anyone about what was happening to these women? Ever hear him complain to any of the defendants or indeed anyone else about what was happening to these women as they were taken off at the checkpoints?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: When would you next see the women after they were taken off the truck at the checkpoint?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: The next morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did -- what sort of condition would they be in when you saw them the next morning?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exhausted. They looked as if they were drunk from lack of sleep, fatigue.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did the soldiers who put them back on the trucks ever say anything that you overheard? And if you did overhear it, I want to hear exactly what was said. Okay?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: When the truck stopped, Stojan would get off, and they would get in. We were sitting in the truck.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: So this guard would have an opportunity to see them being taken off the truck and being put back on the truck the next day.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: All right. I want to ask you now about some questions about the hotel in Odzak, the hotel in which Mr. Simo Zaric had his office, or apparently had his office, and where you assembled in the mornings to be given your tasks. Do you know a man named Novica Simic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Who is he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think he's a general of the Serbian army, the East Bosnia Corps, something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Did you ever see him in Odzak?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only once.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Where was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Inside the hotel, on one of the floors.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: What were you doing inside the hotel on this occasion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I was repairing taps in the bathroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Tell the Chamber under what circumstances you saw Mr. Simic, Mr. Novica Simic?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, I was just about to say whenever we have a name of somebody else other than the defendant, please use the full name.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay. My question is, Witness, when did you -- under what circumstances did you see Mr. Novica Simic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw him in one of the rooms. The door was slightly open, so when I was passing by that room, I saw one of the girls from my town in the room.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: What was her name? Just before you answer that, just before you answer that, I think we are in open session. Are we not?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. So you want private session?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Just for --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: A few minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: -- For a few minutes while we get this evidence out and then we can resume.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Then we will go back, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: 1.01 p.m., to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 5th day of December, 2001, at 9.30 a.m.
